title: Run the test check through pinned cargo-nextest, with doctests
summary: Retry of the nextest speedup. The Athena `test` check, CI and producer guidance run the suite via a pinned cargo-nextest plus a separate `cargo test --doc`. The goal is faster checks, and the user judges it from docs/decisions.md and later job times. This reading adds what the last attempt missed: ATHENA_HOME in the check env, a wrapper that names its runner, a hard checksum pin, and parsing of nextest output.

defaults_applied.how: Adopt cargo-nextest instead of building a parallel runner; record sccache, shared target dir and splitting as alternatives.
New parsers and wrapper logic get unit tests; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
The decision cites the measured compile/run split and the before medians, labeled as measured by the brain.
Criteria check test counts and failing-test names parsed from nextest output, plus the ATHENA_HOME env, not just file existence.
A missing nextest or a nonzero nextest or doctest exit fails the check by mechanism.
After-medians are measured on later jobs that used nextest.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: faster checks and CI; audience is the user reading docs/decisions.md and later job times.
Measured split from the user (4 cores): compile 67 s, run 673 s warm, so running dominates.

Checks run with a cleared environment (env_clear) passing only HOME, PATH and env_pass_if_set; so ATHENA_HOME = "{athena_home}" must be added to both capability env tables so the wrapper finds the pinned tool.
Per the proposed request, if nextest is missing the wrapper fails the check loudly and does not fall back to cargo test; it prints one line naming the runner used.

The pin checksum must be real. If the producer cannot obtain a verified version and checksum in the sandbox, it stops and reports that, rather than landing an unverified pin; CI install failure must stop CI loudly.
The first real nextest run may only happen in CI or in later jobs; the decision claims no unmeasured after number and says after-medians count only jobs whose check ran nextest.
Files checks.rs, gh.rs and config.rs are legitimately in scope: test-count parsing, failing-test-name parsing and the Tools schema (deny_unknown_fields).
question: Can the producer obtain the real cargo-nextest version and sha256 checksum? If it can't, should the job stop instead of landing an unverified pin?

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md has a new decision recording the measured split (compile 67 s, run 673 s, 4 cores, measured by the brain, slowest binaries listed), the chosen change (pinned cargo-nextest plus cargo test --doc), and at least three alternatives (sccache per D79, shared target dir, splitting slow tests) with reasons.
The decision states the before medians (9.7 min checks, 17.6 min producers, 29 jobs), says after-medians are measured on later jobs whose check used nextest, and claims no unmeasured after number.

athena.toml [tools] pins cargo-nextest by version and a real checksum like the other tools. The test check for change and study uses nextest plus a separate doctest run, with no test filtered or ignored. Both capability env tables set ATHENA_HOME = "{athena_home}".

.github/workflows/ci.yml installs the pinned nextest, failing loudly if the download or checksum fails, and runs nextest and cargo test --doc under one `test` check. CHANGELOG.md has an entry with the measured split.

Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes. The new unit tests show that the nextest summary and failing test names are parsed (checks.rs, gh.rs), that libtest output still works, that a check environment built from the real athena.toml contains ATHENA_HOME, and that a missing nextest or a nonzero exit fails the check with a message naming the runner.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Adopting sccache or a shared target directory
Changing which tests exist or skipping any test
Changing CI routing beyond the single test check
departures: Larger than the reference: a multi-file change across Rust crates, xtask, CI and docs. The real nextest checksum may be unobtainable in the sandbox, and the earlier attempt ran out of planning rounds.
urgent_reason: Cuts the median 9.7 minute check time and the repeat CI suite runs, and avoids another planning-round failure.
